independent_initial_proposal.note: Formed only from the source packet (and the current selected wording that the packet itself carries) before reading decisions.json, notes or GPT/Gemini/Claude records.

Gen.4.7.lexical: שְׂאֵת tagged noun (lemma 7613), formally the qal infinitive construct of נשׂא with no object. Strongest contextual anchor is v5–6 נָפְלוּ פָנֶיךָ (face fell) → "lifting [of face]". Alternatives: acceptance (נשׂא פנים idiom of favor), forgiveness (נשׂא עון), pre-eminence (cf. 49:3 יֶתֶר שְׂאֵת).
Gen.4.7.syntactic: חַטָּאת (fem) with רֹבֵץ (masc ptc) and masc suffixes in תְּשׁוּקָתוֹ / בּוֹ. Preferred: substantival "a croucher" predicated of sin, suffixes agreeing with that masculine image. Alternatives: suffixes refer to Abel; חַטָּאת = sin offering lying at the door. Akkadian rābiṣu comparison is a scholarly comparative proposal, not an attested reading of this text.
Gen.4.7.discourse: Verbal echo with 3:16 (תְּשׁוּקָה + משל ב) — should be mirrored in target languages. Speech begun in 4:6 ends here.
Gen.4.7.modal: תִּמְשָׁל yiqtol: must / can / will. Prefer deontic "must" in conditional-admonition context; record "can" and "will".
Gen.4.7.textual: No variant in the pinned packet. Greek version is widely reported to diverge sharply in this verse; not verified in this run.

proposal.ko: 네가 잘 행하면 낯을 들 수 있지 않겠느냐? 그러나 네가 잘 행하지 않으면, 죄가 문 앞에 웅크리고 있다. 그것의 갈망은 너를 향하지만, 너는 그것을 다스려야 한다.”

Gen.4.8.lexical_syntactic: וַיֹּאמֶר ... אֶל־הֶבֶל אָחִיו normally introduces direct speech; none follows before וַיְהִי. וַיָּקָם ... אֶל = rose against (hostile). בִּהְיוֹתָם בַּשָּׂדֶה temporal.
Gen.4.8.textual: Pinned WLC has no speech and no gap marker in the XML. Ancient versions (Greek, Samaritan, Syriac, Latin; Targumic expansions) are reported in secondary literature to supply "Let us go (out) to the field"; some Masoretic editions are reported to mark a mid-verse section gap here. Neither report verified in this run (network blocked).

findings.finding: Current ko 4:7 "죄가 너를 갈망하지만" turns the nominal clause וְאֵלֶיךָ תְּשׁוּקָתוֹ into a verb with explicit subject 죄, whereas ko 3:16 has "네 갈망은 네 남편을 향하고". The deliberate lexical/syntactic echo (תְּשׁוּקָה + אֶל, משל ב) is visible in en/es but not in ko; the explicit 죄 also closes the Abel-referent alternative more firmly than the Hebrew suffix does.
findings.strength: strongest finding of this review; low-risk wording fix

findings.finding: Acceptance is defensible, but the only in-text anchor is v5–6 "face fell" (rendered 낯빛이 어두워졌다 / face fell / semblante decayó). A face rendering keeps that echo in all three languages. Mild preference only.
es 3:16 "gobernará sobre ti" vs 4:7 "debes dominarlo": same verb משל ב rendered differently; "gobernar sobre él" would keep the echo (pecado is masculine, so él is unambiguous enough).

"spoke to/말을 했다/habló con" slightly smooths אמר אל which introduces speech; "said to/말하였다/dijo a" leaves the gap visible without inserting a modern ellipsis. Low-priority; current wording is not wrong.

strongest_objection_to_own_view: For 4:7 the face rendering is itself an ellipsis-supplement; the Hebrew idiom of a lifted face is fundamentally about being received with favor, which "accepted" states directly and which Korean 낯을 들다 (to be unashamed) may not convey. Three earlier models (GPT, final Gemini) settled on acceptance after cross-review. Hence F2 is only a mild preference and not a requested change.

final_opinion_ko: 현행 채택문은 두 절 모두 원문에 대한 오역이 없고 대안 주석도 충실하다. 가장 실질적인 개선점은 4:7 한국어가 3:16의 "갈망은 ~을 향하고 / 다스리다" 평행을 깨뜨린다는 점(F1)이며, 최소 수정안("그것의 갈망은 너를 향하지만")을 권한다. 스페인어도 3:16과 동사를 맞추는 것(gobernar sobre)을 권한다. שְׂאֵת의 "낯을 듦" 번역과 4:8의 "말하였다/said to"는 약한 선호이며 현행 유지도 정당하다. 4:8에 대사를 보충하지 않는 현행 원칙에 동의한다.
